mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY and UNRATE exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by more than 0.4pp for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 3% over six consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >3% over 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when INDPRO declines by more than 3% over six months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of at least 0.5% in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and a year-over-year increase of at least 2% in Personal Savings (RSAFS) signals improved household formation and savings, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises by >0.5% AND RSAFS rises by >2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes where HOUST rises by more than 0.5% and RSAFS increases by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals a low-rate, high-inflation environment that erodes real yields and compresses equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL rises by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for four consecutive months, without a corresponding decline in payrolls (PAYEMS), signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces corporate earnings and increases downside risk for equities over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for 4 consecutive months AND PAYEMS does not decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE increases (>0.3pp for 4 months) with stable or rising PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline of more than 1% in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 growth adjusted for population) combined with a concurrent decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) of more than 2% signals broad-based demand contraction, which depresses earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 growth falls by more than 1% YoY and INDPRO declines by more than 2%.
